title.en: History: The World between two World Wars

text.en: Meena heard about a time of great hunger and unemployment in the world. "The Great Depression," said her teacher.

The period between the wars (1919-1939) saw big changes. The Russian Revolution of 1917 under Lenin set up a communist state, and Stalin later led the Soviet Union through planned development.
In 1929 the Great Depression began with the stock market crash in the USA. Banks failed and many lost jobs. President Roosevelt's New Deal tried to revive the economy.
Dictators rose in Europe: Mussolini's fascism in Italy and Hitler's Nazism in Germany. Japan expanded in Asia. These aggressive regimes and the failure of the League of Nations led to war.
The period between the wars (1919-1939) saw big changes.
The Russian Revolution of 1917 under Lenin set up a communist state, and Stalin later led the Soviet Union through planned development.
In 1929 the Great Depression began with the stock market crash in the USA.
Banks failed and many lost jobs.
President Roosevelt's New Deal tried to revive the economy.
Dictators rose in Europe: Mussolini's fascism in Italy and Hitler's Nazism in Germany.
Japan expanded in Asia.
These aggressive regimes and the failure of the League of Nations led to war.
Between 1919 and 1939, democracy faced severe tests as economic turmoil, nationalist anger and ideological extremes swept across continents.
In the Soviet Union, after Lenin introduced the New Economic Policy, Joseph Stalin launched Five-Year Plans from 1928 to industrialise rapidly and collectivise farms.
Collectivisation expanded factories and heavy steel, yet forced grain quotas and suppression caused terrible famines and loss of freedom.

board.text: Rapid Soviet industry vs human cost

text.en: In the West, Wall Street's crash in October 1929—Black Tuesday—triggered the Great Depression, wiping out savings and freezing global credit.

board.text: Oct 1929: Wall Street crash starts Depression

text.en: Factories shut, one in four US workers lost jobs, farm prices collapsed, and global trade shrank as countries raised high tariffs.

board.text: Global collapse in jobs, farms & trade

text.en: Colonial India suffered harshly too: raw jute, cotton and rice prices plunged while British land taxes and gold exports crushed peasants.

board.text: Depression hits Indian farmers & Tamil peasants

text.en: From 1933, US President Franklin D. Roosevelt's New Deal created public works, regulated banks, introduced social security and restored confidence.

board.text: Roosevelt's New Deal revives US economy

text.en: Meanwhile, economist John Maynard Keynes urged governments to spend on jobs during downturns instead of waiting blindly for markets to heal.
In Italy, Benito Mussolini founded the Fascist Party with Blackshirt militias, seized power via the 1922 March on Rome, and crushed opposition and trade unions.
Germany's democratic Weimar Republic struggled with Versailles reparations and 1923 hyperinflation until the 1929 Depression threw six million Germans out of work.

board.text: Weimar Republic weakened by crisis & debt

text.en: Adolf Hitler exploited this despair through the Nazi Party, promising jobs, German pride and tearing up Versailles, becoming Chancellor in 1933.

board.text: 1933: Hitler turns Germany into Nazi dictatorship

text.en: The Nazi regime burned books, jailed political rivals in concentration camps, indoctrinated youth, and persecuted Jewish citizens through the Nuremberg Laws.

board.text: Nazi terror, censorship & persecution of Jews

text.en: In East Asia, militarists took control of Japan, invading Manchuria in 1931 and launching full-scale war on China in 1937 for coal, iron and empire.
Fascist aggression escalated when Mussolini conquered Ethiopia in 1935, while Hitler rearmed Germany and occupied the Rhineland in 1936.
During the 1936–1939 Spanish Civil War, Hitler and Mussolini tested bombers for General Franco while democratic powers stood by.

board.text: Spanish Civil War tests Axis weapons

text.en: Why didn't Britain and France stop Hitler earlier? They followed 'Appeasement'—giving in to Hitler's demands to avoid another war and fearing Soviet communism.
At Munich in 1938, Britain and France handed Czechoslovakia's Sudetenland to Hitler, only for Hitler to seize the rest of Czechoslovakia months later.
Even anti-colonial regions stirred during these years—Ho Chi Minh organised nationalism in Indo-China while African and Arab movements challenged European rule.
Then in August 1939, Germany and the USSR shocked the world with the Nazi–Soviet Non-Aggression Pact, clearing Hitler's path to invade Poland.

board.text: Aug 1939: Nazi–Soviet Pact seals Poland's fate

text.en: Compare two responses to 1929: democratic New Deal reforms protected freedoms, while fascist regimes chose dictatorship, censorship and conquest.
Trace the chain: 1929 crash -> mass despair -> rise of Hitler/Mussolini -> appeasement & League failure -> outbreak of WWII.
The inter-war decades proved that defending jobs fairly and stopping aggression early are essential to preserve democracy and peace.

problem.en: How did the Great Depression of 1929 help Adolf Hitler and the Nazi Party win power in Germany?

text.en: Explain the pre-1929 fragility.

why.en: Germany's Weimar democracy relied heavily on US loans to pay reparations and keep factories running.

text.en: Show the 1929 shockwave.

why.en: When Wall Street crashed, US loans dried up overnight, shutting German banks and leaving six million workers unemployed.

text.en: Connect despair to Nazi propaganda.

why.en: Hitler promised work, order and cancelling Versailles, turning desperate voters away from fragile democratic coalitions.

prompt.en: A friend says Roosevelt led Germany's Nazi party. How will you reply?
